subject: Archaeology
title: Flinders Petrie: Father of Modern Archaeology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Flinders Petrie: Father of Modern Archaeology.

hook.text: Before Flinders Petrie, Egyptian archaeology meant treasure hunting. He turned it into science.

buildup.text: Petrie insisted on recording every object's exact position, even broken pottery that others threw away.

discovery.text: He invented sequence dating — using pottery styles to arrange sites in chronological order without texts.

twist.text: Petrie was so obsessed with measurement that he measured the Great Pyramid's stones to 1/100 of an inch.

climax.text: His methods spread worldwide and became the foundation of modern archaeological technique.

punchline.text: The man who saved broken pottery saved archaeology itself.

quiz.question: What technique did Flinders Petrie invent?
options: Sequence dating using pottery styles to establish chronology
Ground-penetrating radar for locating buried structures

details.summary: William Flinders Petrie pioneered systematic archaeological methods in Egypt, insisting on recording every artifact's exact location rather than just extracting treasures. His introduction of sequence dating and pottery seriation transformed archaeology from treasure hunting into science.
details.whyItMatters: Petrie's methods — careful recording, stratigraphy, and artifact classification — became the foundation of modern archaeology worldwide. Before him, excavators routinely destroyed irreplaceable contextual information.
takeaways: Petrie pioneered systematic recording of artifact locations
He introduced sequence dating through pottery seriation
His methods transformed archaeology from treasure hunting to science

faq.question: What was wrong with archaeology before Petrie?
faq.answer: Early excavators focused on finding impressive objects for museums, discarding pottery and recording little about where things were found. This destroyed the contextual relationships between artifacts that give them meaning. Petrie insisted context was as important as objects.

faq.question: What is sequence dating?
faq.answer: Petrie arranged pottery styles in chronological order based on how they changed over time. By tracking these stylistic changes, he could date sites without written records. This seriation method remains fundamental to archaeology, especially for prehistoric periods.
